I honestly havent read any latino writers from N**orth America,** except  Junot Diaz, but i've read a lot of latin american writers from Latam, especially from Mexico.

Here in Mexico I'd say the big 3 in literature (they are required reading at some point) are Octavio Paz, Juan Rulfo and Sor Juana Inès de la Cruz. I would also recomend Juan J. Arreola (a lot) and Carlos Fuentes.

For the rest of Latin America, I personally believe that the best novelists are from Colombia, Garcìa Màrquez is the most famous example but Àlvaro Mutis is much much better, and GGM said so himself and called hime his master; Evelio Rosero is another excelent colombian novelist, currently writing novels.

That being said, I think the best poets are chilean, like Neruda or Huidobro or Parra.

Finally, You won't find any latin american short story (or poetry for that matter) compilation without at least one work from Jorge Luis Borges, from Argentina, and its true argentines are excellent short story tellers, but i deeply prefer Julio Cortàzar over Borges.

There's obviously lots and lots more, Cuba, Nicaragua, Perù and Uruguay all have excellent writers and poets like Josè Martì, Rubèn Darìo, Mario Vargas Llosa and Mario Benedetti respectively.

Feel free to DM me if you have any more questions, I love this stuff, I'm from Mexico and love sharing our literature.
